statement: A digit string of length n is good when every even index (0-based) holds an even digit and every odd index holds a prime digit (2, 3, 5 or 7). The first line holds n. Print how many good strings of length n exist, modulo 1000000007. Even positions offer 5 choices and odd positions 4, and positions are independent, so the answer is 5 to the power of ceil(n/2) times 4 to the power of floor(n/2) - compute both powers with recursive fast exponentiation under the modulus.

example.why: Length 1 has only index 0, which is even, so exactly the digits 0, 2, 4, 6 and 8 qualify.

hint: Apply the modulus after every multiplication inside fast power; the exponents are huge.
mistake: Building the power with a loop of n steps - n reaches 10 to the 15, and only halving finishes in time.
